threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot a newbie when they queue for an hour at the market, oblivious to the pop-up stalls just around the corner with fresher produce.
Caught a night bus by the market, and the guy next to me was arguing with his phone. Thought he lost the plot until I saw the live train updates on his screen.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The random karaoke night at the back of a kebab shop on Sonnenallee, when everyone joined in, even the grumpy old man at the counter.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a 24-hour Kebab stand that doubles as an art gallery. Midnight snack and culture, all in one bite.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a real local by how they grip the BART handrail—less iron grip, more casual lean. Tourists cling on like their life depends on it.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: On the 31 Balboa yesterday, a guy serenaded us with a guitar while a pigeon critiqued his singing from the floor. Classic San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the parks are just for lounging, but locals use them for community events, secret music gigs, and spontaneous petanque games.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their confusion over which side to walk on the narrow sidewalks—locals move in a straight line like they’re part of traffic.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check the train apps for delays instead of just expecting them. Everyone else knows it's part of the experience.
Caught the 333 last night; a guy was singing opera while the driver pretended he didn’t hear. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I found half the people on my street were attending the same spontaneous street party, sharing food and laughter. That's Neukölln magic.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how some cafes here will serve you a shot of espresso and a glass of sparkling water for the same price? It's like a mini service ceremony. Love it!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows that avoiding BART during rush hour is just as important as knowing the best taqueria for those late-night cravings.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 line at 4pm, and the driver announced a spontaneous dance-off after a tech guy spilled his coffee. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia's plazas are just for selfies, but locals actually use them for quick chats and grabbing a croissant from the baker.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still ask for directions at the Placa del Sol instead of just following their phone’s GPS while clutching a coffee.
